quotes.how: parsed with the same routine as scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs#intentCriteria and by scripts/error-boundary-capture.test.mjs#intentCriteria, so every criterionText below is the intent's own text and not a paraphrase; the pin that holds it compares character for character, and scripts/error-boundary-capture.test.mjs reddens on a row whose criterion differs from the intent by one character

why: No row is required, and the list therefore names no driver, no instance and no verdict path: scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs refuses a list with no required row that names a driver, so naming one would be the opposite defect.

The reason is not convenience. A required row must name the driver a control-ai-browsers run expression takes to the wave gate, and that driver must return the gate's four readings — toolElements, drawnRect, descriptor and noDevContext — with the required rows together citing drawnRect, descriptor and noDevContext, because that is the reading set the overlay driver produces. This milestone's readings are the two component types a boundary record carries, the error's own identity, the named absences the join answers and the epoch delta the page agent keeps — none of which a page element's rect or dev context can produce. Naming spikes/probes/overlay-pick.js as their driver would make the gate return overlay measurements for boundary criteria, which is the re-cut N6 forbids; a boundary driver does not exist in this repository and this task may not add one.

The portal is not lost by that ruling: it is the subject on which every positive half of this milestone is an absence — 0 provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners(), 0 ErrorHandler subclasses, 0 boundary directives, the stock ErrorHandler resolved and no onViewError on it — and the recording, the join and the pane are what turn those absences into answers. Every row above names the artefact that carries it and the command that proves it.

claims.criterionText: When a boundary catches an error, the finding names the component whose template threw it from the hook record's own `declarationType`, names the component that declares the boundary from `details.boundary.type`, and reports the two as separate facts alongside `caughtBy` and a reset reported as available only when the record carries one; a subject that declares no boundary produces cannot-tell with the named absence `no-error-boundary-declared`, naming no boundary, no declaring component and no reset.
claims.asserts: A boundary that caught an error yields one finding naming the component whose template threw it from the record's own declarationType, naming the component that declares the boundary from details.boundaryType, reporting the two apart beside caughtBy and a reset reported as available only where the record carries one; a subject that declares no boundary is cannot-tell with no-error-boundary-declared, naming no boundary, no declaring component and no reset.
claims.artefact: research/raw/m042-error-boundary.json (hook.details.paths[0] detectChangesInView: declarationInstance, declarationType, caughtBy, boundary; hook.details.paths[1] boundaryConstruction: the same four fields with no caughtBy; hook.details.measured.keys; hook.retainedState.fields: error and the host view only) -> extension/error-boundary.js (findingOf, rule 1 and rule 4) -> apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-error-boundary.ts
claims.proves: node --experimental-strip-types --test "extension/error-boundary.test.mjs" (E1, E2) and node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/panel-error-boundary.test.mjs" and npx nx run angular-ai-devtools:test (panel-demo.spec.ts holds the pane's sample fact to the recording)
claims.reason: The two component types can only differ on a page that declares a boundary, and the portal declares none: 0 provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners(), 0 ErrorHandler subclasses and 0 boundary directives in the portal checkout, so no insurance-portal route produces the declaring-versus-throwing pair this criterion is written on, and CHARTER.md's portal clause therefore has no page-side fact of this criterion to reach. What carries the claim is research/raw/m042-error-boundary.json — the hook record's two details shapes, read from the fixture installation of @angular/core 22.2.2 and quoted from S10 where only a page could measure them — joined by extension/error-boundary.js and rendered by apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-error-boundary.ts. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "extension/error-boundary.test.mjs", whose E1 pins render the two types apart and refuse an invented parent and whose E2 pins render no-error-boundary-declared with no boundary, no declaring component and no reset; scripts/panel-error-boundary.test.mjs holds the same separation at the pane. A portal-backed verdict would return the portal's own absence, which is E2's answer and not the positive half this criterion names.

claims.criterionText: The finding reports the error the boundary received — the thrown value's own `name` and `message`, and its `cause` when the boundary wrapped a value that is not `Error`-like — and never any text read from the rendered `@error` view, so a fallback whose text differs from the thrown message is reported as fallback content and never as the error; an installed hook that has caught nothing in the window under inspection is cannot-tell with `no-error-caught`, and the view reader asked for facts with no `@error` view in the DOM is cannot-tell with `no-error-view-rendered`.
claims.asserts: The finding reports the thrown value's own name and message, and its cause only where the boundary wrapped a value that is not Error-like, and never any text the rendered @error view carried; a fallback whose text differs from the thrown message is reported as fallback content; an installed hook that caught nothing is cannot-tell with no-error-caught and a view reader with no @error view in the DOM is cannot-tell with no-error-view-rendered.
claims.artefact: research/raw/m042-error-boundary.json (hook.wrapped: encapsulateBoundaryError and ErrorBoundaryWrappedError with its cause; hook.errorView.keys ["$error","$reset"]; hook.fallback: primary false, fallback true, text "caught: S10 spike: thrown inside the @boundary primary view"; hook.quotations at s10-answer.md:140-144, :148-151, :169-175) -> extension/error-boundary.js (findingOf, fallbackOf, errorViewOf) -> apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-error-boundary.ts
claims.reason: The portal never throws into a boundary, so no insurance-portal route produces the disagreement this criterion is about — a thrown message and a rendered fallback that say different things — and none renders the finding either: the surface that reports the error is served from apps/angular-ai-devtools, which inspects the page rather than being it. CHARTER.md's portal clause therefore has no route whose facts this criterion names. What carries the claim is research/raw/m042-error-boundary.json, where the wrapping class, the wrapped cause, the @error context keys and the probe's rendered text are each quoted with the source anchor that carries them, joined by extension/error-boundary.js and rendered by apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-error-boundary.ts. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "extension/error-boundary.test.mjs", whose E4 pin requires the thrown name and message and requires the rendered text in no finding field, whose E5 pin keeps no-error-caught and no-error-view-rendered distinct, and whose E6 pin reports a non-Error throw as the boundary's own wrapper with its cause and an Error as itself; scripts/panel-error-boundary.test.mjs holds the fallback to its own field at the pane.

claims.asserts: An error that reaches the handler without ErrorDetails is cannot-tell with no-boundary-details, names no boundary, no declaring component and no caught-by mechanism, and is never rendered as "the app kept no error".

CHARTER.md's portal clause therefore does not reach the criterion's own fact. What carries the claim is research/raw/m042-error-boundary.json, whose two details shapes are read from the installed chunk with their reader sites, joined by extension/error-boundary.js, which answers no-boundary-details for a handler delivery and never "the app kept no error". The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "extension/error-boundary.test.mjs", whose E7 pin renders no-boundary-details with no boundary and no caught-by and refuses to let that absence overwrite a record that also carries a boundary; scripts/panel-error-boundary.test.mjs holds the same absence at the pane.

claims.reason: The portal is exactly the subject this criterion is written on — it declares no provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners(), its provider list is apps/insurance-portal/src/app/app.config.ts:23-39 with no error provider at all — but what the portal produces is the absence, not the answer: the cannot-tell that names no-global-error-listeners is the join's and the panel's, served from apps/angular-ai-devtools, so CHARTER.md's portal clause has no route that renders the criterion's own fact. The absence itself is not lost: it is what the second half of the claim rests on. What carries the claim is research/raw/m042-error-boundary.json, which records the provider the fixture declares and the listener sites the install registers, and the shipped page agent's own walk, which answers declared or no-global-error-listeners rather than a boolean. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/error-boundary-capture.test.mjs", whose held-out E10 pin drives one raw window error through the shipped agent on two subjects — one whose injector carries the global-listeners token and one whose injector does not — and requires the finding through the handler on the first and cannot-tell carrying no-global-error-listeners on the second, with neither rendered as no errors occurred.

claims.reason: This criterion is about the instrument, not about a portal route: it is answered by driving the shipped extension and the project gate, and no insurance-portal route produces a test run or an extension-thrown error, so CHARTER.md's portal clause has no portal fact to reach — a portal-backed verdict would still be evidence about a page rather than about the extension's own throw. What carries the claim is extension/agent-main.js's guarded epoch read, which is measured in both directions: research/raw/m042-error-boundary.json records the epoch delta a keyed identity still names and the delta a non-keyed identity must not keep, and the frame that used to be lost now lands. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "extension/agent-main.test.mjs", whose E12 pin records zero agent-thrown TypeErrors on a load and a reload while the epoch record still names every changed epoch id it named before the repair, and whose E13 pin records the same across two loads in one session without attributing one page's epoch change to the other; scripts/error-boundary-measure.test.mjs re-derives the recording those pins quote. The project gate itself is npm run check && npm test, recorded in T006's Log and in .project/build/verify-ledger.jsonl rather than claimed here.
